chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Appreciation versus envy among musicians (second pass)
summary: Repeat of his view that soloists were praised in the thirties and that envy grew in the fifties.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Now you were saying before when we were talking about the way the big band would stop and then your band would take off, what was that?
Whatever tune they played, we'd pick it up.
Yeah. Did this ever make them
mad or did they feel you were trying to outdo them or was there always this spirit of competition?

This was a period of appreciation of what somebody else did. This new phase of people being envious of one another playing instruments. That wasn't in existence then. A guy in the band or on a bandstand that played a beautiful solo, his fellow musicians would give him the accolade that he deserved. You know.

The band, we had a period of superior talent like when, say the Duke Ellington band, when the guys would turn their backs, I don't know, I'm not going to name any names because they are all friends of mine --

But they would turn their backs on a fellow soloist you know, because "I am the great I am" and that is a later development of the jazz scene and during the period of my coming up under that scene, if a guy played a beautiful solo, you told him.
You know, and the next time he played solo, he would play it better, and you'd feel better you know? But no, everybody became a specialist, you know. And it became an envied thing --
When do you think that started
Ah, I'd say in the fifties.
Because then rock and roll was in. I mean, all of those teenagers, the Meltones, and so-and-so tones and all these tones and Allan Freed and all that stort of stuff.
The vocal groups with the names like Orioles and --

Yeah, I mean most of those, and the thing that hurts me most is that it was a matter of survival so we didn't get the pension, the social security sort of bit that would be profitable to me now because we got paid on the spot.
